biggestGap: Brock is in on his own jokes: about twenty lines end on a dry, knowing fragment ('Very blurry.', 'Great cat.', 'Long story.', 'Doesn't count.', 'Allergic, but fit.'), so he is both the dog and the narrator undercutting the dog. Scott never knows he is funny. He ends on a sincere, wrong, delighted conclusion ('this makes way more sense!', 'pretty cool for a god of torture!') and leaves the undercut to someone else. In the next pass, rewrite those deadpan-button lines so each ends on Brock's earnest wrong belief, said as a cheer or a plea, and hand the dry undercut to the star's reaction.

notes:
Head to head, round 4. Bar character: Scott Howl (sincere, loud, athletic golden retriever who wants to help and belong; never mean). The Monster Prom reference file existed and was read in full, along with charm-notes.md.

OUR 12: (1) Ma'am! My intentions are cardiovascular. Also emotional. Mostly cardiovascular. Home by nine. Stretched. (2) I gave {rival} a thumbs up an hour ago. No thumb back. I'm still holding it. (3) Good game. Good game. Line up, everybody, handshakes. Why is nobody lining up. (4) Hi, nine, ten, sorry, I count when I'm nervous, eleven, twelve. (5) Prince emailed me twelve times tonight and I answered all twelve and he panicked. He didn't have a next email. (6) Bye! Can someone cheer me off? I'll start. You join. Let's go, BROCK. Anybody. (7) That's fine, that's totally fine, I'm fine, why is my leg doing that. (8) Sorry in advance. You'll say we need a break. I'll hear rest day. I'll be two towns away. (9) Why me? Ask Denise. Eighty-one, deadlifts her grandson. Grandson's forty-four. He books it weekly. (10) Dash, buddy, my user Kyle tried your funnel and he's still in it. We lower sandwiches down. (11) I've been waiting for this since walk-on, I did lunges the whole time, I can't feel my legs, hi. (12) Vex knows what you want before you do. She told me what I want. A nap. Take it BACK.

SCOTT'S 12: 'Half of my friends are balls, actually! There's Ollie the volleyball, Fergus the golf ball, Troy the basketball...'; 'I also used to have Barry the Beachball... It wasn't a very healthy relationship.'; 'You're, like, the smartest person I know!' / 'Oh, did I say smart? I think I meant best at coming up with weird plans.'; 'Cool! Can we pretty-please borrow your cage?'; 'Yay, thank you! You're pretty cool for a god of torture!'; 'Cool, okay! I understood... a couple of those words... Let's do whatever you just suggested!'; 'GASP! That's crazy! I thought they were solved by smart people, but this makes way more sense!'; 'Wolf-Scott isn't as smart as Me-Scott!'; 'GRRRR, WHO AM I? AM I HANDSOME?'; 'If there are two wolves there, maybe it won't be so weird!'; 'Wow! You really think that will work? It just kinda looks like paper.'; 'Bro, I need your help! Prom night is going to be a nightmare!'

(a) VOICE: bar. With names covered, all 12 Scott lines are Scott by shape: an interjection opener (Cool!/GASP!/Wow!/Bro), a sincere misreading, and a delighted wrong conclusion. About 7 of our 12 are Brock by shape (the count leak, 'why is my leg doing that', 'Line up, everybody', 'Anybody.', the lunges run-on). The other 5 (Prince email, Kyle funnel, Denise, the thumbs up, the Ma'am line) are Brock by topic, built on the wry, full-stopped deadpan the whole cast shares; Crumb or Maximilian could say them in a fitness costume. Brock has no verbal tic as strong as Scott's 'Cool!' or 'pretty-please'. 'Buddy' only goes to rivals and 'LET'S GO' appears once.
(b) CONSTRUCTION: ours. Our top 12 are tighter than Scott's: the punch word sits last, nothing explains itself, and the details are exact (grandson books it weekly, lower sandwiches down). Scott's lines ramble ('Half of my friends are balls...' trails off) and lean on the narrator for the turn.
(c) QUOTABLE: tie. 'My intentions are cardiovascular' and 'I'm still holding it' clip as well as 'pretty cool for a god of torture'. Scott's ball-friends relationship drama is the stronger out-of-context bit, but our best three hold up.
VERDICT: bar, on voice. The craft is now level or better line by line, but Brock is a well-built joke machine with a dog's topics, while Scott is a person who cannot help being Scott.

Progress since round 3: the race lines and the 'X now' buttons are gone, the breathless run-on and the one-breath plea now carry about a third of the bank, and the generic share fell from 34.8% to 33% even though stillness and 'still stuck' are now counted as templates. The remaining generic weight sits in the twists (rhyme, three-words, truth-lie, worst-trait, budget-date) and in the duplicate notification and subscription beats. Method: 37 of 112 lines are listed, 31 as generic, stock, self-explaining or cast-swappable, plus 6 that are counted only for belonging to a saturated template (stillness, or 'still stuck in it'). The best members of those templates (the thumbs up, Kyle's funnel, Crumb's warm paw) are left off the list on purpose, so the writer cuts the others instead.
